result.summary: Do not dispatch yet: the scheduled-run safety claim is false, and the RED-proof plan does not reach the CLI gate. The 54-hour and 55-hour worked cases check out.

findings.title: Scheduled dreams can legitimately exceed the loud threshold
findings.body: O1 explicitly excludes scheduled runs from its false-positive residual, but schedule.js:1080-1087 accepts any positive integer watchdog timeout. run-job.js:501-504 therefore permits a ten-hour watchdog; config.js:59-64 independently permits eight-hour preprocessing with a twenty-minute lock deadline. A contender after seven hours can encounter legitimate scheduled work and trigger S4. This also invalidates S5's half-hour lookback as a sufficient check for scheduled activity: an older scheduled dream may still own the lock. Deleting it can expose its scratch to another run. This is an incorrect safety premise, beyond the already-priced human-error residual.
findings.recommendation: Qualify the watchdog claim to default configuration, price scheduled overruns alongside attended overruns, and remove the half-hour shortcut from S5 and its mirrors. Require checking for any currently running dream regardless of start time.

findings.title: [Machinery] The declared proof suite cannot exercise S4 under the specified test split
findings.body: The deliverables assign S1–S3 to dream-lock.test.js and S4–S5 to the integration suite, but require every proof to use dream-lock.test.js. AC7 nevertheless requires a mutation of S4's CLI comparison to redden. The lock suite imports only the lock helpers; scripts/red-proofs.js:964-994 executes only the declared suite. Under this split, changing the CLI comparison leaves that suite green, so the required S4 proof cannot become PROVEN.
findings.recommendation: Allow a second proof declaration targeting tests/integration/dream.test.js for S4, or explicitly assign executable S4 coverage to the declared unit suite. Update the permission boundary and AC7 consistently.
